title: Ukrainian
description: Everyday Ukrainian in Cyrillic with transliteration: greetings, family, food, numbers, travel and your day.

units.title: Greetings
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
tips: 'Привіт' (pryvit) is informal; 'добрий день' (dobryi den') is the polite hello.

units.title: People and family
units.description: Talk about the people around you.
tips: There is no 'a' or 'the', and 'is' is left out: 'Він мій друг' = He (is) my friend.

units.title: Food and drink
tips: 'І', 'ї', 'є' and 'ґ' are Ukrainian letters: 'їм' (yim) means 'I eat'.

units.title: Numbers
units.description: Count from one to ten, ask prices and tell the time.
tips: After 2, 3 and 4 a noun changes form: 'чотири яблука' (chotyry yabluka, four apples).

units.title: Travel and directions
units.description: Find your way around a new city.
tips: 'Ліворуч' and 'праворуч' mean left and right; 'де' (de) means where.

phrases.e: The station is on the right.
I am going to the airport.

units.title: Daily routine
units.description: Home, work, school and the time of day.
tips: 'Вранці' (vrantsi) means in the morning and 'вночі' (vnochi) means at night.

phrases.e: I drink coffee in the morning.

units.title: Shopping
units.description: Ask for things, prices and how to pay.
tips: 'Можна карткою?' (mozhna kartkoiu?) is the short way to ask if you can pay by card.

answers: Can I pay with a card?
Can I pay by credit card?
